segmentation.text: An operator of a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway
shall give all signals by hand and arm in the manner required
by NRS 484B.420 [DEF-NRS-484B-420],
except that the operator may give a signal for a right turn by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter.

elements.justification: The three defined terms are admitted aggregates (DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Each is claimed as one atom, never expanded; the 'not a stand-in for' clause excludes only a named class with its own atom and a relational role, and 'operator' is read through the device's controlled motion (agency reading), not as a role atom.

Roadway (DEF-NRS-484A-220, not an aggregate): 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'; st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', the same extent; it is not the sidewalk. rel.occupies anchors the subject: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'. Same mapping as the index's 'upon a roadway' (NRS_484B_627_2).

Every signal the operator gives must be given by hand and arm: sig.hand_signal is 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning in {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}', and a signal given by other means is sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state in {off, left, right}' (read as a signal, never as the turn, so its 'not a stand-in for' clause does not apply). The manner is borrowed from DEF-NRS-484B-420 (s4): 'All signals given by hand and arm shall be given by hand and arm extended beyond the left side of the vehicle in the following manner, and shall indicate the turns that follow: (1) Left turn: Hand and arm extended horizontally. (2) Right turn: Hand and arm extended upward. (3) Stop or decrease speed: Hand and arm extended downward. (4) Reentering lane of traffic from parked position: Hand and arm extended horizontally.' The manner is the arm used and the direction it is extended; sig.hand_signal carries only the meaning of the signal given, so the manner is a gap (below).

The exception permits a right-turn signal given with the right hand and arm extended horizontally to the right side of the device. sig.hand_signal carries the meaning 'right' of a signal given, not which arm is extended nor in which direction, so a right-arm horizontal signal cannot be told from a left-arm upward one or from a non-conforming posture: the posture is the gap (below).

compositions.quote: All signals given by hand and arm shall be given by hand and arm extended beyond the left side of the vehicle in the following manner, and shall indicate the turns that follow: (1) Left turn: Hand and arm extended horizontally. (2) Right turn: Hand and arm extended upward. (3) Stop or decrease speed: Hand and arm extended downward. (4) Reentering lane of traffic from parked position: Hand and arm extended horizontally.

applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate, its footprint overlaps a roadway, and it gives a signal at the observation: its turn indicator is left or right, or its arm signal has a meaning other than no_signal.
obligation: Every signal the subject gives is given by hand and arm: its arm signal has a meaning other than no_signal wherever its turn indicator is lit; and the arm signal is given in the posture DEF-NRS-484B-420 states for its meaning (left arm extended beyond the left side: horizontally for left or re-enter, upward for right, downward for stop or slow), except that a right-turn signal may instead be the right hand and arm extended horizontally to the right side. The posture is not carried by any atom (gap); the node is not coded until the gap is resolved.

narrowings.why: 'operator' is read through the device's controlled motion on the roadway, whoever controls it, as the ontology's reading of who controls a road user's motion states.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides on a roadway with its turn indicator showing right and its arm signal no_signal throughout: a signal is given otherwise than by hand and arm.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on a roadway, turn indicator off, gives an arm signal of meaning left with the left arm extended horizontally beyond the left side.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a sidewalk, off any roadway, and gives an arm signal: the duty does not arise.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter on a roadway shows its turn indicator right; the source does not observe arm signals.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on a roadway gives a right-turn arm signal with the right hand and arm extended horizontally to the right side of the bicycle (the exception).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on a roadway gives an arm signal of meaning right with the left arm extended horizontally beyond its left side, a posture DEF-NRS-484B-420 gives to a left turn.

gaps.proposal: `sig.hand_signal_posture` | the posture of a driver's or rider's arm signal: **arm** in {left, right}, the arm extended; **side** in {left, right}, the side of the vehicle or device beyond which it is extended; **direction** in {horizontal, upward, downward}, the direction the hand and arm point **Not a stand-in for:** the meaning of the signal (`sig.hand_signal`), which a source may decode from different postures | general
gaps.nearest: sig.hand_signal: its contract carries 'the meaning of the one given' only, not the arm, side or direction of the extension, which is the manner the duty requires (the action the law requires: which arm and which direction).

gaps.proposal: `sig.hand_signal_posture` | the posture of a driver's or rider's arm signal: **arm** in {left, right}, the arm extended; **side** in {left, right}, the side of the vehicle or device beyond which it is extended; **direction** in {horizontal, upward, downward}, the direction the hand and arm point **Not a stand-in for:** the meaning of the signal (`sig.hand_signal`), which a source may decode from different postures | general
gaps.nearest: sig.hand_signal: meaning 'right' is the same for the right arm extended horizontally to the right and the left arm extended upward; the exception turns on which posture is used, which its contract does not carry.

segmentation.text: Every person operating a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway shall, except:
(a) When traveling at a lawful rate of speed
commensurate with the speed of
any nearby traffic;
(b) When preparing to turn left;
or
(c) When doing so would not be safe,
ride as near to the right side of the roadway
as practicable,
exercising due care
when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction.

For purposes of paragraph (c) of subsection 1, the conditions under which it is not safe to operate a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable include, without limitation:
(a) When fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals or surface hazards impede access to the right side of the roadway.
(b) When a lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregates of the three defined terms, each claimed as one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded into classes; 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion (agency reading), not as a role atom, which the aggregate's 'not a stand-in for' clause excludes.

'upon a roadway': st.roadway is 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-220 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder'; rel.occupies anchors the subject ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). As in the index ('upon a roadway', NRS_484B_627_2). 'shall, except:' introduces the exceptions of this roadway duty. The words of exception (b) name no place for the left turn; a left turn off a roadway is made where it meets another way, so the declared intention is read at every kind of region where that happens: st.intersection ('the region where two roadways meet') and st.driveway_or_alley_entrance ('private road, alley or driveway meeting the highway'), the latter covering every alley, driveway and private road entrance.

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'), one ru.aggregate atom. 'any nearby traffic' is every road user of that aggregate, other than the subject, whose body gap to the subject (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') is within the nearby reach, whatever its direction of travel; where none is nearby the comparison holds vacuously ('any'), the subject then holding back no traffic. surface_gap is the body gap itself, not a centre distance.

The right side of the roadway is its right edge: st.road_edge, 'curb or edge of the roadway', lying on the same highway (st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway its kind) as the roadway the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.roadway). Nearness is the gap between the subject's body and that edge: prim.region_lateral_offset is 'the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', negative for an edge on the right, less half the subject's width from kin.extent ('a formula reads the full length, width and height'); st.region_geometry carries the edge's outline the primitive reads, and its 'not a stand-in for occupancy' clause does not apply, occupancy being read by rel.occupies. Same family of atoms as the index's 'drive to the extreme right side of the highway' (NRS_484B_627_1a), here on the roadway's edge.

Things that impede access to the right side: 'fixed or moving objects', 'animals' and 'surface hazards' are st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user; kind in {debris, excavation, hose, barrier, stalled_vehicle_wreckage, sidewalk_fixture, mail_drop_box, other}' (an animal that is not ridden or herded is such an object, kind other); 'parked or moving vehicles', 'bicycles' and 'pedestrians' are the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle and DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian, whatever their motion. Impeding access is the thing lying in the rider's way on its right side: for an object, ahead of the subject along the designated direction of the roadway it occupies within the reach (prim.region_offset_along, 'the signed distance (m) from a road user's reference point to a structure region ... measured along a carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction)', from zero to the reach) and at or to the right of the subject (prim.region_lateral_offset at or below zero), its outline being st.region_geometry; for a road user, the body gap (rel.surface_gap, 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the reach, ahead and at or to the right of the subject (rel.bearing, 'direction of b from a in a's frame'). Neither atom is used for a clearance it excludes: surface_gap is the body gap itself; bearing is a direction only.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed commensurate with the speed of nearby traffic
operationalizations.convention: Traveling is the subject's speed (kin.speed) above the source's speed resolution (p.halt_speed_tolerance). The subject's speed is commensurate with the nearby traffic (s4b: traffic road users within p.nearby_traffic_reach, two seconds of headway at urban speed) where each such road user's speed exceeds the subject's by no more than p.commensurate_speed_margin, a speed differential within one traffic stream; the bound moves with both measured speeds.

operationalizations.standard: when doing so would not be safe
operationalizations.convention: Not safe is read through the two conditions subsection 2 names: (a) an object, vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian on the subject's right within p.right_side_impede_reach (s13), the distance within which a rider must steer around it; (b) the lane the subject occupies narrower than p.shared_lane_min_width (s14), the wide-outside-lane width of bicycle facility guidance below which a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot share a lane side by side.

operationalizations.standard: as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable
operationalizations.convention: As near as practicable is a gap between the subject's body and the roadway's right edge of at most p.bicycle_keep_right_gap: a bicyclist's shy distance from a curb or edge plus the sway of its operating space and the source's position error (AASHTO bicycle operating space).

operationalizations.standard: the conditions under which it is not safe ... include, without limitation
operationalizations.convention: The catch-all 'include, without limitation' is read only through the contracts s13 and s14 read: obstructions and road users of the named aggregates on the subject's right within p.right_side_impede_reach, and a lane narrower than p.shared_lane_min_width.

operationalizations.standard: a lane too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane
operationalizations.convention: The lane the subject occupies (rel.occupies, st.lane) has a width (st.lane_width, 'width of a lane at a point') below p.shared_lane_min_width: 14 ft, the lane width below which bicycle facility guidance (AASHTO, MUTCD shared-lane guidance) holds that a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot travel safely side by side within one lane; the bicycle and the vehicle are the design road users the width stands for, not road users present in the scene.

applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate and its footprint overlaps a roadway at the observation, and none of the exceptions holds there: (a) the subject is traveling (speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), complies with NRS_484B_785_1a (its lawful speed), and every road user of the traffic aggregate other than the subject whose body gap to it is within p.nearby_traffic_reach has a speed no greater than the subject's plus p.commensurate_speed_margin (vacuously true where no such road user is nearby); (b) for some intersection or driveway/alley entrance r, the source's declaration current at the observation states int.left_turn for the subject at r; (c) not safe: some obstruction o lies ahead of the subject within p.right_side_impede_reach along the designated direction of a roadway the subject occupies (prim.region_offset_along from zero to the reach) with a lateral offset from the subject at or below zero (on its right or overlapping its line), or some road user of the vehicle, bicycle or pedestrian aggregate other than the subject has a body gap to the subject within p.right_side_impede_reach and a bearing whose longitudinal component is positive and lateral component at or below zero, or the subject occupies a lane whose width is below p.shared_lane_min_width.
obligation: At the observation the subject rides as near the right side of the roadway as practicable: with r a roadway the subject occupies, for some road edge e lying on a highway on which r lies, with e's lateral offset from the subject negative (on its right), the magnitude of that offset less half the subject's width (kin.extent) is at most p.bicycle_keep_right_gap. Where no road edge on a highway of r lies on the subject's right in the scene, or the offset is unobserved, the verdict is unknown (definedWhen), never violated.

narrowings.why: 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion on the roadway, whoever controls it.

The catch-all 'include, without limitation' is read only through the contracts s13 and s14 read: obstructions, and road users of the vehicle, bicycle and pedestrian aggregates, in the rider's way on its right, and a lane narrower than the shared-lane width; other unsafe conditions, among them road users of no named aggregate (electric bicycles and electric scooters, which the vehicle and bicycle definitions leave out), are not read.
The right side is read relative to the subject's heading (the primitive's frame), and the edge is a mapped road edge on a highway the occupied roadway lies on.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides at 5 m/s on a roadway whose outside lane is 5.0 m wide, its body 2.5 m from the right road edge; a car of the vehicle and traffic aggregates travels the same way at 13 m/s with a body gap of 20 m behind it; no obstruction or other road user is on its right, no intersection or driveway entrance is in the scene, so no left turn is declared.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the bicycle rides with its body 0.6 m from the right road edge.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a sidewalk, its footprint overlapping no roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source maps regions without their outlines, so the road edge's lateral offset from the bicycle is unobserved.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides alone at 5 m/s in the middle of a 5.0 m outside lane; no other road user is in the scene, so exception (a) holds vacuously: the duty binds the subject alone and is decided.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the outside lane is 3.5 m wide, below the shared-lane width (exception (c), s14).

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but a parked car of the vehicle aggregate stands 10 m ahead of the bicycle on its right, at the curb (exception (c), s13).

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but an intersection lies ahead and the source declares int.left_turn for the bicycle at it (exception (b)).

scenarios.name: branch_5
scenarios.narrative: An electric scooter rides at 8 m/s, above the speed NRS_484B_785_1a allows it, 2.5 m from the right edge of a 5.0 m lane; a car travels the same way at 9 m/s 20 m behind it: its speed is commensurate but not lawful, so exception (a) fails.

param_proposals.name: p.bicycle_keep_right_gap
param_proposals.convention: the gap between a bicycle or scooter rider's body and the right-hand curb or roadway edge within which the rider counts as riding as near to the right side as practicable: the shy distance a bicyclist keeps from a curb or edge plus the sway of its operating space and the source's position error
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist operating space and shy distance)

param_proposals.name: p.nearby_traffic_reach
param_proposals.convention: the gap between bodies within which another road user counts as nearby traffic: two seconds of headway at an urban speed of about 15 m/s
param_proposals.source: two-second following rule of driver manuals

param_proposals.name: p.commensurate_speed_margin
param_proposals.convention: the amount by which the speed of nearby traffic travelling the same way may exceed a rider's speed with the rider still counted as keeping pace with it: about five miles per hour, the speed differential within which road users travel as one stream
param_proposals.source: speed-study practice (5 mph speed bins, Highway Capacity Manual platoon definitions)

param_proposals.name: p.right_side_impede_reach
param_proposals.convention: the gap between a rider's body and an object or road user on its right within which that object impedes the rider's access to the right side of the roadway: about three seconds of travel at a bicyclist's cruising speed of 5 m/s, the distance within which a rider must steer around it
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist speed and reaction distance)

param_proposals.name: p.shared_lane_min_width
param_proposals.convention: the lane width below which a bicycle and a motor vehicle cannot travel safely side by side within the lane: 14 ft, the wide outside lane width of bicycle facility guidance
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities; MUTCD shared-lane guidance

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: sensor speed resolution of the acquisition standard

segmentation.text: Every person operating a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
upon a roadway shall, except:
(a) When traveling at a lawful rate of speed
commensurate with the speed of
any nearby traffic;
(b) When preparing to turn left;
or
(c) When doing so would not be safe,
ride as near to the right side of the roadway
as practicable,
exercising due care
when passing a standing vehicle or one proceeding in the same direction.

For purposes of paragraph (c) of subsection 1, the conditions under which it is not safe to operate a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter as near to the right side of the roadway as practicable include, without limitation:
(a) When fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, bicycles, pedestrians, animals or surface hazards impede access to the right side of the roadway.
(b) When a lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a vehicle to travel safely side by side within the lane.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregates of the three defined terms, each one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded; 'person operating' read through controlled motion (agency reading).

st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', is the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-220; rel.occupies anchors the subject ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'), as the index maps 'upon a roadway'. The exceptions 'except:' introduces qualify the keep-right duty (sibling spans, see PLAN).

'passing ... a vehicle' from the rear is drv.interaction.overtake_pass: 'Road user a overtakes and passes road user b from the rear: a, travelling in the same direction as b, comes from having b ahead of it to having b behind it'; its contract 'says nothing of ... whether b moves', so it covers a standing and a moving b. 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle. 'standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-250, not an aggregate): 'the halting of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than for the purpose of and while actually engaged in receiving or discharging passengers', read as b at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation'), the passenger purpose being unobservable (observable_reading purpose). 'one proceeding in the same direction' is b moving (kin.speed above the tolerance) with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned').

operationalizations.convention: Due care is a standard of the rider's state of mind; it is bounded by the clearance kept while passing. At every observation of the pass at which the two bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) the bodies do not touch (rel.contact) and the lateral component of their body gap (rel.surface_gap) is at least p.door_swing_reach where the passed vehicle is at rest (the reach of a door opened into the rider's path) and at least p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap where it moves (the bicyclist's operating-space sway beyond its body width); the bound is selected by the passed vehicle's motion at each such observation.

applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate, and at the observation drv.interaction.overtake_pass(subject, b) is recognized (window p.overtake_window, heading tolerance p.overtake_same_direction_cos) for some road user b of the vehicle aggregate, the subject's footprint having overlapped a roadway at some observation since the act began.
obligation: For each such b: at every observation since the act began (the last observation of the window behind at which b was ahead of the subject with headings aligned) up to the recognition at which the two bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero), rel.contact between the subject and b is false and the lateral component of rel.surface_gap is at least the clearance selected there: p.door_swing_reach where b is at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance), p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap where b moves with its heading aligned with the subject's (rel.same_direction, p.overtake_same_direction_cos). Surrogate: the verdict is evidence of care, not a legal conclusion.

narrowings.why: 'person operating' is read through the device's controlled motion, whoever controls it.
'standing' is read as the passed vehicle at rest: the definition's exclusion of a halt for receiving or discharging passengers turns on a purpose no atom observes, so every halt is read as standing.
Due care, the whole obligation, is read only as the clearance kept and the absence of contact while alongside the passed vehicle; the rider's attention and its speed while passing are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on a roadway overtakes and passes a car of the vehicle aggregate parked at the curb (at rest throughout), keeping a lateral body gap of 0.4 m while alongside it.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the bicycle keeps a lateral body gap of 1.5 m while alongside the parked car.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides alone along a roadway and passes no road user: no pass is recognized.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe the gap between bodies.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on a roadway passes a car moving slowly the same way, keeping a lateral body gap of 1.2 m while alongside it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle on a roadway passes a car moving slowly the same way, touching its mirror while alongside it.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on a separate path beside the roadway as the pass of a parked car begins and moves onto the roadway part way through the pass, keeping a lateral body gap of 0.4 m while alongside the car: the subject was on the roadway at some observation of the pass.

scenarios.name: branch_4
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides on the roadway, then moves onto a separate path off the roadway before the parked car comes ahead of it, and passes the car from the path with a lateral body gap of 0.4 m: it was on the roadway only before the pass began.

param_proposals.name: p.door_swing_reach
param_proposals.convention: lateral reach of an open passenger-car side door beyond the vehicle body (a front door opens about 0.9 to 1.1 m)
param_proposals.source: passenger-car door dimensions (door-zone guidance for bicyclists)

param_proposals.name: p.bicycle_pass_safe_gap
param_proposals.convention: the lateral clearance between the body of a passing motor vehicle and a bicyclist's: the bicyclist's operating-space sway beyond its body width, about one metre of free space beside it
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (bicyclist operating space)

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: sensor speed resolution of the acquisition standard

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_window
param_proposals.convention: the longest duration of an overtaking manoeuvre on an urban street, from having the overtaken vehicle ahead to having it behind

param_proposals.name: p.overtake_same_direction_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest heading difference (about 25 degrees) at which two vehicles count as travelling in the same direction while one moves out to pass the other

segmentation.text: Persons riding bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters
upon a roadway
shall not ride more than two abreast
except on paths or parts of roadways set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles, electric bicycles and electric scooters.

elements.justification: Admitted aggregates of the three defined terms, each one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded; they class the subject and the other riders the obligation counts. 'riding' is read through the device's motion (agency reading).
st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder', the extent of DEF-NRS-484A-220; rel.occupies anchors the subject. As the index maps 'upon a roadway'.

Riding abreast is riding side by side in a row: rel.longitudinal_overlap, 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)', at or above zero; travelling the same way, rel.same_direction, 'headings aligned'; in one row, the body gap rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies') within the spacing of riders side by side. Riding is moving: not drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation'). More than two abreast is the subject and two other riders of the s1 aggregates so placed. longitudinal_overlap is used as the projection it is, not as a contact or distance; surface_gap is the body gap itself.

'paths or parts of roadways set aside for the exclusive use of bicycles, electric bicycles and electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; rel.occupies anchors the subject on it: the riding the words except is the subject's own riding, on such a facility. The three device words name the users the facility is reserved for, the kind's own contract, not road users the duty counts.

applicability: The subject is a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate, is moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt with p.halt_speed_tolerance), its footprint overlaps a roadway, and it overlaps no bicycle lane or path at the observation.
obligation: At the observation there are no two road users b and c, distinct from each other and from the subject, each a member of the bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter aggregate and moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt), such that for each of the three pairs among subject, b and c the bodies are side by side (rel.longitudinal_overlap at or above zero) with headings aligned (rel.same_direction, p.side_by_side_same_direction_cos), and at least two of the three pairs have a body gap (rel.surface_gap) at most p.abreast_gap_max.

narrowings.why: 'Persons riding' is read through the devices' controlled motion, whoever controls them.

Abreast is read as side by side, travelling the same way and in one row, the row being two of the three pairs within the riders' side-by-side spacing; riders side by side but lanes apart are not abreast.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Three bicycles ride side by side at 6 m/s on a roadway outside any bicycle lane, headings aligned, body gaps of 0.5 m between neighbours.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle rides alone on a roadway: no other rider is in the scene, and the duty is decided for the subject alone.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Three bicycles ride side by side on a sidewalk, overlapping no roadway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but the source does not observe the longitudinal overlap of bodies.

scenarios.name: branch_1

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in an ordinance enacted pursuant to NRS 484A.469 [DEF-LVMC-11-40-185-A],
an electric scooter
may be operated:
On a roadway, bicycle lane, path or route
at a speed of not more than 15 miles per hour.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter, claimed as one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'); the named class ru.electric_scooter is not substituted for it.

'roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'; 'bicycle lane, path' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; a 'route' for these devices runs on roadways and paths, so it adds no place beyond them. rel.occupies anchors the scooter on them. 'bicycle' here names the structure kind, not road users the duty counts.
kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity' (m/s), compared with the law's own figure, a literal; its 'not a stand-in for' clauses concern no other quantity here.

residues.why: The ordinance the words name (LVMC 11.40.185(A), posted as DEF-LVMC-11-40-185-A: 'an electric bicycle or an electric scooter may be operated on a public roadway or sidewalk, or a lane, path, or route designated for bicycle, electric bicycle, or electric scooter use') provides where a scooter may be operated and states no speed; nothing in it provides otherwise on the speed this line bounds, so the duty is the same whether or not the exception's words hold.
The permission to operate adds no restriction to the speed bound: a scooter at rest or moving below the bound meets it alike, so the duty is the same whether or not the scooter is being operated.

applicability: The subject is a member of the electric scooter aggregate and its footprint overlaps a roadway or a bicycle lane or path at the observation.
obligation: The subject's speed (kin.speed) is at most the literal 15 mph at the observation.

narrowings.why: The permission 'may be operated ... at a speed of not more than 15 miles per hour' is read as its limit: operation on these places above the figure is outside what the line permits.

segmentation.text: A vehicle
shall not be driven over
any unprotected hose
of a fire department
when laid down on any highway or private way or place
for use at any fire or alarm of fire or practice runs,
without the consent of the fire department official in command.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one ru.aggregate atom ('membership of a legal aggregate'), never expanded.

Driven over the hose: the vehicle's footprint overlaps the hose's region (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') while it moves, not drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation'); the hose is st.obstruction of kind hose, the region the relation reads. 'be driven' is read through the vehicle's motion (agency reading).

A hose lying on a way is st.obstruction, 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user; kind in {..., hose, ...}'. 'unprotected' distinguishes a bare hose from one covered by a hose bridge or ramp, which the contract does not carry: gap below.

The hose's belonging to a fire department is a status no feature on the road displays apart from the hose itself: the hose of kind hose lying on the way is read as the fire department's (observable_reading status).

The purpose for which the hose is laid (a fire, an alarm, a practice run) is not observable; it is read through the hose laid on the way, the feature that purpose explains (observable_reading purpose).

The nearest carrier of consent is a direction to proceed given by a person directing traffic: dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic and the direction given; role in {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; indication in {stop, proceed, slow, turn(dir)}', governing (dev.governs) the travel region the vehicle occupies. Its roles do not include the fire department official in command, whose consent the exception requires: gap below.

residues.why: 'any highway or private way or place' names every place a hose can lie: the duty is the same wherever the hose is laid down.

applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate, is moving (not drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance), and some obstruction of kind hose lies in the scene at the observation.
obligation: The subject's footprint does not overlap any obstruction of kind hose that is unprotected (not covered by a hose bridge or ramp: gap), unless the fire department official in command gives consent, read as that official directing traffic to proceed over the region the subject occupies (gap). The node is not coded until both gaps are resolved.

narrowings.why: 'be driven' is read through the vehicle's motion over the hose, whoever controls it.
A hose lying on the way is presumed the fire department's: no feature displays its owner.
The purpose of laying the hose is read through the hose laid on the way.

gaps.proposal: `st.protected_hose` | a hose lying on or across a way that a hose bridge or ramp covers, so that a vehicle crossing it does not bear on the hose; a region with a boundary, coinciding with the covered stretch of an `st.obstruction` of kind hose **Not a stand-in for:** a bare hose (`st.obstruction` kind hose without this cover), or a barrier | general
gaps.nearest: st.obstruction kind hose: its contract records 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user' and its kind, not whether the hose is protected; whether driving over it is forbidden turns on that distinction (the action the law forbids).

gaps.proposal: `dev.fire_official_direction` | the fire department official in command at a fire scene directing road users, and the direction given; **indication** in {stop, proceed}, with `dev.governs` relating it to the travel regions it controls **Not a stand-in for:** a police officer's, flagger's or crossing guard's direction (`dev.human_direction`) | general
gaps.nearest: dev.human_direction: its role attribute is one of {police_officer, flagger, school_crossing_guard, railroad_flagger}; the consent of 'the fire department official in command', which decides whether the vehicle may drive over the hose, is none of them.

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
upon a highway
of this State,
subject to exceptions with respect to parked vehicles as stated in chapters 484A to 484E, inclusive, of NRS,
must display lighted lamps and illuminating devices
as respectively required in this chapter for different classes of vehicles:
(a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise;
(b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead;
and
(c) When directed by an official traffic control device.

elements.justification: The admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one ru.aggregate atom, never expanded.

Highway (DEF-NRS-484A-095, not an aggregate): 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'; st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', not the roadway; rel.occupies anchors the vehicle. As the index maps 'upon any highway'.

Lighted lamps displayed: sig.headlamp, 'headlamp state in {off, low_beam, high_beam}', lit (low or high beam), and sig.position_lamp, 'position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit'. As the index maps 'The lights required by this Section shall be burning' (LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2).

env.darkness, 'insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter': the period from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise is the darkness period whose boundary the reading sets at the law's figure, declared as a literal. As the index maps 'during the period from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise' (LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2).

Insufficient light is env.darkness ('insufficient natural light'); unfavorable atmospheric conditions are env.visibility, 'visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)', below the law's 1,000 feet. As the index maps the same words (LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2).

The nearest carriers of a device directing lamps on are dev.regulatory_sign (a catalogue of codes with no lamps-on code) and dev.zone_sign (kinds with no daytime-headlight zone), governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) the vehicle occupies; neither carries the direction: gap below (the open gap smoke31-1111-0039:G21 on these words).

residues.why: Every highway a reading of this corpus judges lies in this State, the jurisdiction the corpus is applied in; the words add no restriction a trace of the reading could fail.

Which lamps and illuminating devices each class of vehicle must carry (number, colour, mounting) is set by the chapter's equipment sections, which are not lines of this corpus and which no atom carries; the display duty is carried on s5 as headlamps and position lamps lit.

applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate, its footprint overlaps a highway, NRS_484D_165_3 does not apply to it (ruleApplies false), and at the observation (a) env.darkness holds, or (b) env.darkness holds or env.visibility is below the literal 1,000 ft, or (c) an official traffic control device governing the region it occupies directs lamps on (gap).
obligation: The subject's headlamps are lit (sig.headlamp low_beam or high_beam) and its position lamps are lit (sig.position_lamp). The node is not coded until the gap on s10 is resolved.

narrowings.why: The lamps each class must display are read as headlamps and position or tail lamps lit; the per-class equipment is not read (s6 residue).

gaps.proposal: `dev.lamps_on_sign` | a regulatory sign directing road users to display lighted lamps (headlamps on) where it governs, with `dev.governs` relating it to the travel regions it controls and the same structured **conditions** attribute as `dev.zone_sign` **Not a stand-in for:** whether lamps are lit (`sig.headlamp`) or whether it is dark (`env.darkness`) | general
gaps.nearest: dev.regulatory_sign: its catalogue of codes has no lamps-on direction; dev.zone_sign: its kinds include no headlight zone; whether the device directs lamps on decides when the display is required (the time of the duty).

segmentation.text: Whenever a vehicle is parked or stopped
upon the traveled portion of a highway or shoulder adjacent thereto,
whether attended or unattended
during the times mentioned
and there is insufficient light to reveal any person or object within a distance of 1,000 feet upon such highway or roadway,
such vehicle shall display lighted lamps
meeting the requirements of subsection 1 [(1) appended below].

Every vehicle shall be equipped with one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle.
The location of such lamps shall be such that at least one such lamp is installed as near as practicable to the side of the vehicle which is closest to passing traffic.

elements.justification: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one ru.aggregate atom. 'parked or stopped' is the vehicle at rest, drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation'), which covers a parked vehicle and one stopped for any time; as the index maps 'stopped or parked' (NRS_484B_450_1l).

'the traveled portion of a highway' is st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder' (as the index maps 'the paved or main-traveled part of the highway'); 'shoulder adjacent thereto' is st.shoulder, 'the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic', lying on the same highway (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on'; st.highway its kind, 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'). rel.occupies anchors the vehicle on either.

The times are borrowed from NRS-484D-100-1 (t5): '(a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead;' read as env.darkness ('insufficient natural light; the boundary relative to sunset and sunrise is a reading parameter') or env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)') below the same 1,000-foot figure as t6. The third circumstance of that line, a device directing lamps on, is not borrowed: the condition t6 joins by 'and' entails time (b), so the times hold wherever t6 holds, whatever that circumstance is.

Insufficient light to reveal a person or object within 1,000 feet: env.darkness ('insufficient natural light') or env.visibility ('visibility distance (fog, dust, smoke)') below the law's figure, a literal; as the index maps the like words of LVMC_11_38_120_B_o2.

The lamps subsection 1 (t8) describes are borrowed from the appended text: 'one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle'. These are the parking lamps to the front and the tail lamps to the rear: sig.position_lamp, 'position, parking, cowl or tail lamps lit (the lamps a vehicle shows without its headlamps)'. Their colour, reach and location are residues (t9, t10).

compositions.why: The words borrow only the periods NRS 484D.100 names (darkness from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise; other times when insufficient light or atmospheric conditions make persons and vehicles not discernible at 1,000 feet) to say when this duty arises; nothing turns on whether that line's lamp duty applies to this vehicle or is complied with, and that line itself excepts parked vehicles, so composing it would read its exception, not its times.
compositions.quote: (a) At any time from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise; (b) At any other time when, because of insufficient light or unfavorable atmospheric conditions, persons and vehicles on the highway are not clearly discernible at a distance of 1,000 feet ahead;

compositions.why: The words borrow from the appended subsection 1 only its description of the lamps (front lamps showing white or amber, rear lamps showing red) to say which lamps the displayed lights are; the equipment duty of subsection 1 need not be complied with for this display duty to be judged, and it is no node of the corpus.
compositions.quote: one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a white or amber light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the front of the vehicle, and one or more lamps which, when lighted, shall display a red light visible from a distance of 500 feet to the rear of the vehicle

residues.why: 'whether attended or unattended' covers both states: the duty is the same whether or not anyone attends the vehicle.

The equipment duty and the lamps' colour (white or amber to the front, red to the rear) and reach (visible from 500 feet) describe the lamps the obligation requires displayed; no atom carries a lamp's colour, reach or fitment, so the rule reads only that the position lamps are lit.
The location of the lamps (one as near as practicable to the side closest to passing traffic) is a fitment requirement no atom carries; the rule does not read it.

applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate, at rest (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance), its footprint overlaps a roadway or a shoulder lying on the same highway as a roadway, and at the observation env.darkness holds or env.visibility is below the literal 1,000 ft.
obligation: The subject's position lamps are lit (sig.position_lamp) at the observation.

narrowings.why: The lamps the appended subsection describes are read as the position (parking and tail) lamps lit; their colour, reach and location are not read (residues on t9 and t10).

segmentation.text: Any lighted headlamps
upon a parked vehicle
shall be depressed or dimmed.

elements.justification: sig.headlamp, 'headlamp state in {off, low_beam, high_beam}': lighted headlamps are a state other than off.

'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, one ru.aggregate atom. 'parked' is drv.motion.parked, 'Road user a is parked: "the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not", observed as a at rest at every observation of the window behind', as the index maps 'parked' (NRS_484B_473_2).
Depressed or dimmed headlamps are the low beam: sig.headlamp state low_beam, not high_beam; as the index maps 'such lights shall be depressed or dimmed' (NRS_484B_473_2).

applicability: The subject is a member of the vehicle aggregate, drv.motion.parked holds for it (speed tolerance p.halt_speed_tolerance, duration p.parking_min_duration), and its headlamps are lit (sig.headlamp low_beam or high_beam) at the observation.
obligation: The subject's headlamps are on low beam (sig.headlamp low_beam) at the observation.
